full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff-petitioners filed the suit for setting aside the decree dated 30.11.76 obtained by the defendant in Title Suit No. 55 of 1975 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, Sylhet for specific performance of contract against vendor Provashini Bala Das who was the original owner of the property. The plaintiffs' case is that they purchased the suit property by a registered kabala on 5.6.72 from Provashini Bala Das and are in possession. The plaintiffs were not aware of the said suit filed by the defendants and the decree in that suit was obtained by collusion and non-service of summon upon them. The plaintiffs having come to know for the first time in the month of Chaitra, 1385 B. S. about the ex pate decree filed the suit. 

 6. The main contention of the plaintiffs was that the ex parte decree was obtained by suppression of summons and on the contrary the defendants asserted that the summons were duly served on the plaintiffs. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division found from service return Ext. 1, dated 22.8.72 and the hajiras Exts. Neo and Neo(1) dated 17.8.72 and 19.9.72 respectively that the plaintiffs filed hajira in that suit and plaintiffs had knowledge about the suit. Apart from that, the plaintiffs through their own uncle Hamdu Miah filed a suit for specific performance of contract being Title Suit No. 69 of 1973, that is about one year after the suit of the defendant in respect of the same self suit land against the common vendor Provashini Bala Das and in that suit the present respondent No. 1 was added as defendant No. 2. The suit of Hamdu Miah was dismissed and ultimately the appeal was dismissed due to non-prosecution. Further the plaintiffs also filed two pre-emption cases, being Miscellaneous Case Nos. 57 and 58 of 1979 in which written statements were filed by the plaintiffs wherein they asserted about the pendency of the present suit. In that view of the matter, the learned Single Judge found that the plaintiffs knew about the pending suit much earlier and they willfully did not appear in the suit. The learned Single Judge further found that the defendants got a kabala registered in pursuance of the previously instituted suit against the common vendor. In that view of the matter, simple suit for setting aside the decree without filing a regular suit for cancellation of registered deed obtained through court is not maintainable. 

 7. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Advocate cited the case of Abdur Rashid and another Vs. Abdul Bari and another, 35 DLR(AD) 162. The decision cited is not very material for our purpose. The reported decision is a case under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, but the present case is in respect of a title suit wherein the material finding of the trial court that the plaintiffs were aware of the suit and they willfully did not appear in the case. Further, the learned Single Judge found that a simple suit for setting aside an ex parte decree is not maintainable without a prayer for cancellation of the registered deed.
